item.title: Version 1.10.0
item.description:
ScoreSort 1.10.0

This update contains a lot of improvements to the Combine tab, and a few bug fixes in the rest of the app.

🔗 Combine — major new feature: Booklets!

  • Booklets. Switch the output menu at the bottom left from Single pages to Booklet, and every part is laid out as its own fold-and-staple booklet — the whole folder in one print job, instead of one document at a time. Full size prints multiple A4 parts onto A3 paper. (You can also print in A5 onto an A4 booklet if you want to.) Each copy of a part becomes its own booklet, and short parts are padded out to a whole folded sheet automatically. Two-page parts are laid out flat — both pages side by side on one sheet — so you can open them on the stand and never turn a page mid-piece.
  • Choose where the page turns fall. When creating a booklet, you can specify how to arrange the pages for sensible page turns. When in booklet mode, try the Page Turns (⌘T) button to view each part and specify where you want to place your page breaks.
  • Booklet page scale. Published music rarely matches A4 exactly, so a Scale box beside the output menu sizes each page within its half of the sheet — above 100% to fill more of the page, below it for more space around the music.
  • Two-sided printing setup. macOS doesn't let an app choose your two-sided setting, and printers differ in which edge they turn the paper on. Set Up Two-Sided Printing… in the output menu prints one numbered test sheet: fold it, say whether the pages came out the right way up, and ScoreSort sets the rest for you, remembered for each printer you use.
  • Print without saving first. A new Print… button (⌘P) sends the combined PDF straight to the print dialog in one step, alongside Create PDF and Open in Preview.

🔗 Combine — other improvements

  • Press Space to look at a file in the list. Quick Look opens on the file you've got selected, just like in Finder — arrow keys move to the next part, Space or Escape closes it again.
  • The Presets button now looks like a button, and stays visibly switched on while the presets panel is open.

🐞 Fixed

  • Renamer: switching ensemble works every time. After the first change, picking a different ensemble moved the buttons but carried on matching against the previous ensemble's instruments — so on Orchestra, an Oboe or Violin part could come up "not recognised" because it was still checking the Jazz Band list.
  • Split: keyboard navigation works again. Clicking an output file left the arrow keys unable to page through the PDF, and in Step 2 Tab jumped to a preview arrow instead of the next instrument name. Sorry!
  • ⌘W now closes the window as you'd hope — it previously did nothing.
  • One View menu instead of two. The menu bar had two menus both called View; the tab shortcuts now live in the standard one alongside Full Screen.

item.title: Version 1.9.0
item.description:
ScoreSort 1.9.0

✨ New: the Stamp tool

  • Add a small text overlay to your parts — "Example School Band", "Property of the Music Dept" — the way you'd use a rubber stamp. Design and save any number of stamps (⌘5), one per school or ensemble.
  • Set the text and style — font, size, colour, and bold or italic on just the words you choose — plus an optional box around it.
  • Put it anywhere on the page: click one of nine quick positions, or drag the stamp around on a live preview of your own part.
  • Type {date} or {year} for a copy date, filled in when the stamp is applied — day-first by default.
  • Stamp files you already have (PDFs and images), a folder at a time, replacing the originals or saving copies under names you type.
  • Stamps are burned into the page, so they print everywhere and can't be deleted out of the PDF.

🔗 Combine

  • New Stamp button in the toolbar — stamp the combined PDF as it's created, on every page or just the first page of each part.
  • Presets can carry a stamp: applying your ensemble's preset arms its stamp.
  • Fixed: clicking a file now selects just that file (it used to behave as though ⌘ was held), and ⌫ removes selected files again.

✂️ Split

  • New Stamp button in Step 1, with the stamp shown on the preview of pages that will get one.
  • More instruments in the naming suggestions (alto/bass flute, oboe d'amore, cor anglais, clarinet in B♭ and A, drum kit, vibraphone, mallet percussion, and a combined "Trombone Baritone Bassoon" part), with spelling variants treated as one instrument.
  • A tidier Step 1 toolbar and consistent headings across all three steps.

item.title: Version 1.8.0
item.description:
ScoreSort 1.8.0

✨ General

  • Many more keyboard shortcuts! ⌘O/⌘S/⇧⌘P/⌘⌫/⌘R now do what you might expect them to. In the combiner, ⇧⌘P pushes you out to Preview, ready to print with ⌘P. You can also always open the folder you're working in with ⇧⌘F. See the Help menu for a full Keyboard Shortcuts reference.
  • Redesigned menu bar — proper File / View / per-tab Actions menus now cover much more of the app's functionality.
  • Many more significant but invisible changes under the hood.

✂️ Split

  • Jazz naming suggestions overhauled.
  • Return / Escape to move between steps with the keyboard.
  • It's now easier to promote unmatched files in Step 3 using the arrow keys.

🔗 Combine

  • Preset sidebar now live-syncs with Preferences.
  • Much smarter preset matching between the side panel and the files you've dragged in (abbreviations/aliases are now understood, clef-precise euphonium, "Clarinet" ≠ "Bass Clarinet").
  • Collate groups get their own colour, distinct from your selection colour.

item.title: Version 1.7.0
item.description:
ScoreSort 1.7.0

✨ General improvements

  • Drop a new file onto the “Done” screen to start the next job immediately, without clicking Start Over (Rename, Bulk Rename, and Split).

🏷️ Rename Files

  • Batch renaming. Rename multiple folders of pieces at once — drag in a parent folder of nested folders, or several folders together, and the app walks you through them one after another.
  • You can now rename image scans (e.g. JPGs) as well as PDFs.

🔗 Combine PDFs

  • Drag to reorder files. Collate groups move as a unit, and you can drop a file onto a group to add it in.

✂️ Split PDF

  • Undo/redo while splitting. ⌘Z / ⌘⇧Z undo and redo split-point, skip, and re-stride edits in Step 1.
  • Drag to pan the part preview in the naming step (the page strip or its minimap), not just the arrow buttons.
  • Much smarter instrument-name suggestions, now driven by the selected ensemble (Wind Band / Jazz Band / Orchestra): suggestions follow that ensemble’s real score order (e.g. Horn follows Trumpet in a band), use ensemble-aware part counts, prefer full instrument names, and handle the clarinet family and baritone/euphonium better.
  • Duplicate-name warning when two files would get the same name; saving is blocked if they’d truly collide.
  • General improvements to the score-order prefix screen.

🐞 Fixed

  • Keyboard shortcuts are now strictly limited to the current tab.
  • The part-name preview no longer clips the instrument name at the top of the page.
  • Dragging a new PDF onto the splitter’s “Done” screen no longer leaves a blank Step 1 preview.

item.title: Version 1.6.0
item.description:
ScoreSort 1.6.0

New

  • Splitter — move the original to Trash. A new checkbox on Step 2 cleans up the source PDF after your split files are saved. Off by default, remembered between uses, and recoverable (it goes to the Trash).
  • Splitter — A3 page preview. The "which half comes first?" dialog now shows a preview of your actual page behind the left/right selector.

Improved

  • Easier-to-hit “Clear” buttons in every tool.

Fixed

  • The app no longer quits from the update dialog at launch.
  • No “check for updates automatically?” prompt on the very first launch.

item.title: Version 1.5.2
item.description:
ScoreSort 1.5.2

Reliability fix: automatic updates now install correctly. (Earlier versions couldn't complete an in-app update — please update manually this once, and future updates will be automatic.)

item.title: Version 1.5.1
item.description:
ScoreSort 1.5.1

A small polish update:

  • Expanded the Welcome Tour — clearer guidance for combining (images, blank pages, table of contents) and splitting, including A3 sheet splitting and booklet reordering.
  • Tidied the default window size and minor UI refinements.
